1.explanation: The Select component (in Select.js) is where the arrow icon is rendered: it picks up theme.select.icons.down and then renders <SelectIcon color='brand'/>. On the dark theme (dark.js) the global icon color is hard-coded to the textColor (#eeeeee) and the ‘brand’ color mapping doesn’t override it, so the icon ends up blending into the dark background and disappears. Fixing this requires adjusting Select.js to pass the correct fill/stroke prop (or a different theme color key) to the SVG icon, or updating the dark.js theme.icon.color or theme.select.icons.down color definition so the arrow shows up against dark backgrounds.
1.bug_scenario: When using a Select inside a dark background (dark-1) theme, the down‐caret arrow icon disappears. In the screenshot on dark purple (dark) background the arrow is not visible, whereas on a light background it renders correctly.

2.explanation: The Select component’s render() method instantiates the down-arrow via <SelectIcon color='brand' />, but on the dark theme the brand or default icon color ends up matching the dark background (or isn’t overridden), so the arrow isn’t visible. The Select class (in Select.js) is where the icon color is applied, and the dark theme (dark.js) doesn’t supply a contrasting select.icons.down color. Fixing either the render() call to use a contrasting color (e.g. theme.global.colors.text) or extending the dark theme to include theme.select.icons.down will restore visibility.
2.bug_scenario: When placing a Grommet Select inside a dark-themed container (background “dark-1”), its down-arrow icon disappears — in the screenshot you see the placeholder “small” on a nearly black background but no visible arrow. On a light background the same Select renders its arrow correctly.
